t:
(a) No Reservation of Water Rights.—Nothing in this subtitle—
        (1) establishes a reservation in favor of the United States with respect to any water or water right on the land transferred by this subtitle; or 
        (2) to authorize the appropriation of water on the land transferred by this subtitle except in accordance with applicable State law.  
    (b) Effect on Previously Acquired or Reserved Water Rights.—
        (1) In general.—Nothing in this subtitle affects any water rights acquired or reserved by the United States before the date of enactment of this Act on the land transferred by this subtitle. 
        (2) Authority of secretary.—The Secretary of the Navy may exercise any water rights described in paragraph (1).

fable.w: The section is a savings clause on water rights: it reserves no new federal water rights, preserves existing ones, and lets the Secretary of the Navy exercise them. The tempting reading is that the reference to "applicable State law" amounts to coordination with states, but it only sets the governing legal standard. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government.
fable.s: to authorize the appropriation of water on the land transferred by this subtitle except in accordance with applicable State law

opus.w: This section is a savings clause. It preserves existing federal water rights and says that State law governs any new appropriation of water. It sets up no process involving anyone outside the federal government. Referring to 'applicable State law' sets the legal standard to follow; it is not consultation or coordination with a State before a federal decision. The only actor named is the Secretary of the Navy, a federal official.
opus.s: (2) Authority of secretary.—The Secretary of the Navy may exercise any water rights described in paragraph (1).
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** One tempting reading is that "except in accordance with applicable State law" brings the State into a federal decision. It doesn't. The phrase only says that State water law governs any appropriation of water. It does not require the federal government to consult the State, hold a hearing, take comments or give anyone a right to object. The only actor named is the Secretary of the Navy, who is inside the federal government. The section is a savings clause about water rights.

qwen_chat.w: The section defines the scope of federal water rights and states that any appropriation of water must be in accordance with applicable State law. It does not require the federal government to consult with state or local governments, nor does it establish any mechanism for outside participation in federal decision-making. Compliance with state law is a legal constraint, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section mentions "State law" and "water rights," it implies some form of coordination with state authorities. However, the text merely states that federal actions must comply with existing state law; it does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from state or local governments before making a decision. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or consultation requirement mentioned.
